extracted.subtask_description: A Wikipedia article summarizing the 1984 action-comedy film Beverly Hills Cop: its plot, production, release, box office, critical reception, awards, and legacy. Intended as an encyclopedic reference about this specific film.

rubrics_metrics.name: Worldwide box office gross
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as a primary commercial-success metric; the article states the film 'grossed $316.4 million worldwide, making it the highest-grossing film released of 1984 in the US.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Domestic box office ranking / year-topper
rubrics_metrics.description: Made the film the highest-grossing film released of 1984 in the US.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page treats 'highest-grossing film of 1984 in the US' as an indicator of the film's commercial prominence for the release year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Box-office longevity (weeks at number one)
rubrics_metrics.description: The film 'stayed at number one for 13 consecutive weeks and returned to number one in its 15th weekend, making 14 non-consecutive weeks at number one.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Length of time at number-one box-office position is presented as evidence of sustained popularity; the article notes a tie with Tootsie for most weeks at number one.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ticket sales estimate
rubrics_metrics.description: Box Office Mojo estimates the film sold over 67 million tickets in the US.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ticket-sales estimates are presented as another measure of audience reach beyond dollar grosses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theatrical release breadth and opening performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Released December 5, 1984 in 1,532 theaters, debuted first place making $15.2 million in its first five days, and later expanded to 2,006 theatres.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Number of theaters, opening gross, and expansion strategy are used in the article to contextualize the film's commercial rollout and success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critical reception / contemporary and retrospective reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: The film 'received positive reviews' and 'in retrospective reviews ... has been appraised by newer critics for its blend of action and comedy.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Qualitative critical commentary from reviewers (e.g., Janet Maslin, Richard Schickel) and retrospective appraisal are treated as measures of artistic/critical success; the article includes both praise and dissenting opinions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rotten Tomatoes approval rating and critics consensus
rubrics_metrics.description: On Rotten Tomatoes the film holds an approval rating of 83% based on 58 critics; critics consensus: 'The buddy cop movie continues its evolution unabated with this Eddie Murphy vehicle that is fast, furious, and funny.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aggregated critic approval percentage and consensus blurb are cited as quantified indicators of critical reception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Metacritic score
rubrics_metrics.description: Metacritic assigned the film a score of 66 out of 100, based on 12 critics, indicating 'generally favorable' reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weighted-average aggregator scores are used as another quantified summary of critical response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awards, nominations, and industry recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: Nominated for Academy Award for Best Original Screenplay; nominated for Golden Globe Award for Best Motion Picture – Musical or Comedy; won People's Choice Award for Favorite Motion Picture; soundtrack and other awards/nominations are listed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Award nominations and wins (Academy, Golden Globes, People's Choice, Grammys, BAFTA, Edgar Allan Poe Awards, etc.) are presented as formal industry measures of quality/recognition for specific aspects (screenplay, soundtrack, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection for preservation (National Film Registry)
rubrics_metrics.description: The film was selected for preservation in the United States' National Film Registry by the Library of Congress as being 'culturally, historically, or aesthetically significant.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inclusion in the National Film Registry is cited as a criterion/marker of long-term cultural and historical significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion in curated lists, rankings and institutional collections
rubrics_metrics.description: Appearances on lists and collections such as 'No.22 on Bravo's 100 Funniest Movies of All Time,' 'AFI's 100 Years...100 Laughs – No.63,' 'Empire magazine's list of The 100 Greatest Movie Characters' (Axel Foley No.78), inclusion in Museum of Modern Art permanent collection, and The New York Times' 'The 1,000 Best Movies Ever Made.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Placement on critics'/institutions' 'best' or 'funniest' lists and inclusion in museum collections are used in the article to demonstrate cultural standing and legacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Soundtrack commercial and critical success
rubrics_metrics.description: Soundtrack won the Grammy Award for Best Score Soundtrack for Visual Media and featured three top-10 Billboard Hot 100 singles (including 'Axel F', 'The Heat Is On', 'Neutron Dance').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Soundtrack awards and chart performance are treated as measures of the film's broader cultural/music impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Home-media shipments and home-market performance
rubrics_metrics.description: The film shipped a record 1.3 million videos in the United States on its initial release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initial home-video shipment figures are presented as an indicator of consumer demand and commercial success beyond theatrical release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Franchise viability and sequels/continuations
rubrics_metrics.description: The film 'spawned a franchise that includes three sequels' and later produced further sequels and a 2024 film; a TV pilot was developed but not picked up.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The creation of sequels, attempted TV adaptations, and later installments are listed as evidence of the film's commercial franchise potential and enduring brand value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Production and development notes affecting film's character
rubrics_metrics.description: Extensive rewrites (Daniel Petrie Jr., Danilo Bach), star-driven changes (Eddie Murphy's input), alternate casting/directing choices (Stallone, Scorsese, Rourke, etc.), budget (~$13–14 million), and shooting locations influencing the final film.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While not an evaluative metric per se, the article presents production choices, casting revisions, and creative contributions as explanatory factors for the film's comedic tone and commercial trajectory; these production elements serve as implicit criteria for understanding how the film's style and success were produced.
